William Alves de Oliveira (commonly known as **William Alves** or simply **William**) is a Brazilian professional footballer born on **7 December 1991** in **Goiânia, Brazil**. He primarily plays as a **striker** or **attacking midfielder** and has had a journeyman career, playing in multiple countries across Europe, Asia, and South America.

Here’s a detailed overview of his career and key details:

---

### **Early Career & Youth Development**
- Born in **Goiânia, Goiás**, William began his football journey in Brazil.
- He played for **Atlético Goianiense** in his youth before moving to Europe.

---

### **Professional Career**

#### **1. Early European Career (2010–2014)**
- **2010–2011: FC Luzern (Switzerland)**
  - Signed by Swiss Super League side **FC Luzern** in 2010.
  - Made his professional debut in the **2010–11 Swiss Super League**.
  - Scored **5 goals in 20 appearances** in his first season.
  - Struggled for consistent playing time in his second season (2011–12), making only **10 appearances (1 goal)**.

- **2012–2013: FC Wil (Switzerland, Loan)**
  - Loaned to **Challenge League (Swiss second division) side FC Wil** for the **2012–13 season**.
  - Had a strong season, scoring **12 goals in 28 appearances**, helping Wil avoid relegation.

- **2013–2014: Return to FC Luzern**
  - Returned to Luzern but failed to secure a regular spot, making only **5 appearances (0 goals)** before leaving in January 2014.

#### **2. Move to Poland (2014–2016)**
- **2014: Zawisza Bydgoszcz (Poland)**
  - Signed for **Ekstraklasa (Polish top flight) side Zawisza Bydgoszcz** in January 2014.
  - Scored **4 goals in 14 appearances** in the second half of the **2013–14 season**.
  - Helped the team win the **2013–14 Polish Cup** (his first major trophy).

- **2014–2015: Lech Poznań (Poland)**
  - Transferred to **Lech Poznań** in July 2014 for a reported **€500,000**.
  - Had a strong debut season, scoring **10 goals in 30 league appearances**, helping Lech win the **2014–15 Ekstraklasa title**.
  - Also played in the **UEFA Europa League**, scoring **2 goals in 6 appearances**.

- **2015–2016: Lech Poznań (Struggles & Loan)**
  - Fell out of favor in his second season, making only **10 league appearances (1 goal)**.
  - Loaned to **Korona Kielce** in January 2016, where he scored **3 goals in 13 appearances**.

#### **3. Return to Brazil & Short Stints (2016–2018)**
- **2016: Atlético Goianiense (Brazil)**
  - Returned to his boyhood club **Atlético Goianiense** in mid-2016.
  - Played in the **Série B (Brazilian second division)**, scoring **3 goals in 15 appearances**.

- **2017: América Mineiro (Brazil)**
  - Joined **América Mineiro** in January 2017.
  - Scored **4 goals in 16 Série A appearances** but couldn’t prevent the club’s relegation.

- **2017: Al-Faisaly (Saudi Arabia)**
  - Moved to **Al-Faisaly FC** in the **Saudi Professional League** in July 2017.
  - Scored **5 goals in 14 appearances** before leaving in early 2018.

#### **4. Return to Europe (2018–2021)**
- **2018: Wisła Kraków (Poland)**
  - Signed for **Wisła Kraków** in February 2018.
  - Scored **6 goals in 14 appearances** in the second half of the **2017–18 Ekstraklasa**.
  - Stayed for the **2018–19 season**, scoring **8 goals in 30 appearances**.

- **2019–2020: Jagiellonia Białystok (Poland)**
  - Joined **Jagiellonia Białystok** in July 2019.
  - Scored **7 goals in 31 appearances** in the **2019–20 Ekstraklasa**.
  - Left in January 2020 after falling out of favor.

- **2020: Górnik Łęczna (Poland, Loan)**
  - Loaned to **Górnik Łęczna** for the second half of the **2019–20 season**.
  - Scored **3 goals in 13 appearances**.

- **2020–2021: Wisła Płock (Poland)**
  - Signed for **Wisła Płock** in August 2020.
  - Scored **5 goals in 26 appearances** in the **2020–21 Ekstraklasa**.

#### **5. Later Career (2021–Present)**
- **2021–2022: Radomiak Radom (Poland)**
  - Joined **Radomiak Radom** in July 2021.
  - Scored **6 goals in 30 appearances** in the **2021–22 Ekstraklasa**, helping the club avoid relegation.

- **2022–2023: GKS Tychy (Poland, I Liga)**
  - Moved to **GKS Tychy** in the **Polish second division (I Liga)** in July 2022.
  - Scored **5 goals in 15 appearances** before leaving in January 2023.

- **2023: Return to Brazil (Aparecidense)**
  - Signed for **Aparecidense** in the **Campeonato Goiano (state league)** in early 2023.
  - Played a few matches before leaving.

- **2023–2024: Unattached / Possible Retirement?**
  - As of mid-2024, William Alves has not been linked with a new club, and his career status is unclear. He may be considering retirement or a move to a lower-division team.

---

### **Playing Style & Strengths**
- **Position:** Striker / Attacking Midfielder
- **Strengths:**
  - Good **finishing ability** (especially in the box).
  - Strong **physical presence** (1.85m / 6'1").
  - Decent **link-up play** and hold-up ability.
  - Experience in multiple leagues, adapting well to different styles.
- **Weaknesses:**
  - Inconsistent form, especially in later years.
  - Not the fastest or most technical player.
  - Struggled with injuries and fitness at times.

---

### **Career Statistics (Approximate)**

|------------------------|--------------------------|----------|-----------|
| FC Luzern              | Swiss Super League       | 35       | 6         |
| FC Wil (loan)          | Swiss Challenge League   | 28       | 12        |
| Zawisza Bydgoszcz      | Ekstraklasa (Poland)     | 14       | 4         |
| Lech Poznań            | Ekstraklasa              | 40       | 11        |
| Korona Kielce (loan)   | Ekstraklasa              | 13       | 3         |
| Atlético Goianiense    | Série B (Brazil)         | 15       | 3         |
| América Mineiro        | Série A (Brazil)         | 16       | 4         |
| Al-Faisaly             | Saudi Pro League         | 14       | 5         |
| Wisła Kraków           | Ekstraklasa              | 44       | 14        |
| Jagiellonia Białystok  | Ekstraklasa              | 31       | 7         |
| Górnik Łęczna (loan)   | Ekstraklasa              | 13       | 3         |
| Wisła Płock            | Ekstraklasa              | 26       | 5         |
| Radomiak Radom         | Ekstraklasa              | 30       | 6         |
| GKS Tychy              | I Liga (Poland)          | 15       | 5         |
| **Total (Senior Career)** | **~300+**            | **~80+** |

*(Note: Exact numbers may vary slightly depending on sources.)*

---

### **Honors & Achievements**
- **Polish Ekstraklasa (1):**
  - **2014–15** (Lech Poznań)
- **Polish Cup (1):**
  - **2013–14** (Zawisza Bydgoszcz)

---

### **Personal Life & Trivia**
- **Nickname:** Sometimes called **"William Alves"** or just **"William"** in Europe.
- **Languages:** Speaks **Portuguese** (native) and has learned **Polish** and **English** during his career.
- **Social Media:** Active on **Instagram (@williamalvesoficial)** with occasional posts about his career.
- **Family:** Little is publicly known about his family, but he has mentioned in interviews that his parents supported his football dreams.

---

### **Legacy & Current Status**
- William Alves is a **journeyman striker** who has played in **7 different countries** (Switzerland, Poland, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, etc.).
- While he never became a **superstar**, he was a **reliable goalscorer** in Poland’s Ekstraklasa and had a **cult following** in some clubs (e.g., Lech Poznań fans remember his 2014–15 title-winning season fondly).
- At **32 years old (as of 2024)**, his career may be winding down, but he could still find a role in a lower-division team or as a veteran presence in a developing league.
